subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers join the existing `agents.defaults.userTimezone` contract, or should they remain host-local as currently documented?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible shipped contracts: host-local is documented and already shipped, while memory-core auto-flush and system prompt behavior already use configured user timezone.

options.title: Use `userTimezone` for session-memory
options.body: Update session-memory filenames, fallback HHMM slugs, headers, tests, and docs to use the resolved `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and clarify that session-memory artifacts intentionally follow the gateway host timezone while auto-flush follows user timezone.

options.title: Add a separate memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a dedicated config surface only if maintainers want memory artifacts decoupled from both host timezone and `userTimezone`.

recommendation.title: Use `userTimezone` for session-memory
recommendation.body: Update session-memory filenames, fallback HHMM slugs, headers, tests, and docs to use the resolved `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the clearest current-main history owner for the implicated session-memory handler and docs path.
